title: Prime Check
problem: Given an integer N (1 <= N <= 1000000) on a single line of input, print "Prime" if N is a prime number and "Not prime" otherwise. A prime number has exactly two divisors: 1 and itself. For example, 7 is prime, and 9 is not because 9 = 3 x 3.
starter_code:
# Read an integer N.
# Print "Prime" if N is prime, otherwise "Not prime".

# Write your code here

hints.1: Think about what makes a number not prime, and which of the smallest numbers are special cases.
hints.2: Numbers below 2 are not prime. Otherwise, loop d from 2 while d * d <= N: if N % d == 0 for any d, it is not prime. Testing d * d <= N (rather than stopping just below the square root) makes sure perfect squares are caught, and it is fast enough for large N.
hints.3:
n = int(input())
print('Prime' if n > 1 and all(n % d for d in range(2, int(n ** 0.5) + 1)) else 'Not prime')

failure_explanation: A prime has exactly two divisors, so 1 is not prime and 2 is. If you only test divisors up to the square root, include the square root itself (loop while d * d <= N), or perfect squares slip through as prime. Print the words exactly as shown, with the same capital letters.
